questions.question: ODD-EVEN TRANSPOSITION SORTING:- ¾ Algorithm performs $n/2$ iterations and each iteration will have two phases: $1^{st}$ Phase: called odd-even exchange, value of a in every odd numbered processor (except processor $n-1)$ is compared with the value of a stored in successor processor. Values are exchanged if lower numbered processor contains the larger value. $2^{nd}$ Phase: called even-odd exchange, value of a in every even numbered processor is compared with the value of a stored in successor processor. Values are exchanged if lower numbered processor contains the larger value. 1 ½ Mark Below is the example gives such sorting of 8 values on one-dimensional mesh processor model: Indices: 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 (CSE 607) 8 Page of 2 Initial 7 8 6 4 5 3 2 1 Values: After < < < ___ Odd-even 7 6 8 4 5 2 3 1 | Exchange $|1^{st}$ iter < < < < | Even-odd 6 7 4 8 2 5 1 3 ___ | exchange After < < < ___ Odd-even 6 4 7 2 8 1 5 3 | Exchange $|2^{nd}$ iter < < < < | Even-odd 4 6 2 7 1 8 3 5 ___ | exchange After < < < ___ Odd-even 4 2 6 1 7 3 8 5 | Exchange $|3^{rd}$ iter < < < < | Even-odd 2 4 1 6 3 7 5 8 ___ | exchange After < < < ___ Odd-even 2 1 4 3 6 5 7 8 | Exchange $|4^{th}$ iter < < < < | Even-odd 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 ___ | Exchange 1 ½ MArks Odd-even transposition sort(one dimensional mesh processor array): Parameter n Global i Local $a,t \{$ For$(i=1;i\le n/2;i++)$ For all $P$_{j }, where $0\le j\le n-1$ do { If $j<(n-1)$ and $odd(j)$ then $\{ t\leftarrow$successor(a); successor$(a)\leftarrow \max (a,t); a \leftarrow \min (a,t); \}$ If even$(j)$ then (CSE 607) 9 Page of 2 $\{ t\leftarrow$successor(a); successor$(a)\leftarrow \max (a,t); a \leftarrow \min (a,t); \} \} 2$ Marks } Here $n/2$ iterations are sufficient to sort n elements and llel algorithm has $O(n)$ as time complexity.
